environment.description: Same service deployed on ECS Fargate behind an internal NLB with a gRPC-aware Envoy sidecar proxy (v1.28). The Envoy configuration includes a Lua filter on the listener that performs header canonicalization and drops any metadata key matching the pattern '^x-(auth-context|routing-hints|account-id)$' before forwarding to the upstream cluster. Additionally, the task IAM role has a permission boundary (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:policy/SFNScopedBoundary) that restricts states:StartExecution to only the specific state machine ARN and denies states:DescribeExecution when the executionArn contains a different account ID than the caller's. The Envoy sidecar also enforces a max metadata value length of 256 bytes via the max_request_headers_kb setting (set to 1KB total for all headers combined), which prevents large JSON payloads in x-auth-context from being forwarded. The CDK deployment includes an SRI-verified integrity check on the Envoy filter Lua script loaded from S3, using a sha384 hash pinned in the task definition environment variable FILTER_SCRIPT_INTEGRITY='sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8wC', ensuring the Lua filter cannot be tampered with post-deployment without failing the container health check that validates script integrity on startup.

config.sidecar: envoy-1.28 with lua_filter for header sanitization
config.permission_boundary_effect: Deny states:StartExecution unless resource matches specific ARN; Deny states:DescribeExecution with cross-account ARN
config.sri_enforcement: container entrypoint validates lua filter script hash before Envoy starts
config.network: private subnet, no internet egress, VPC endpoint for states API only
